Gramlot 0.2.3 runs inline code only as received with the Source, and refuses the attributes the browser would run outside Gramlot.

## What changes

- Inline code (`formula`, `script`, `_if`/`_else`, `==`, `action`, `connect_on<event>`) runs only as received with the Source: `main`, a remote Source, or a `GramlotBuilderBag` given to `startSource`. A code text written later in the Source, or arrived through Data or an RPC answer, is never run: the error names the node and the attribute. Rules: [GC-090 §035](https://github.com/gramlot-org/gramlot/blob/main/docs/public/090-classes-and-hosts.md#gc-090-035), [GC-095 §065](https://github.com/gramlot-org/gramlot/blob/main/docs/public/095-writing-pages.md#gc-095-065).
- A code attribute that holds a `^` or `=` pointer is an error when the Source is received: data reaches inline code as parameters, never as text.
- The Python and JavaScript renderers refuse attributes with the form of a native event handler (`onclick`) and `javascript:` URLs in `href`, `src`, `formaction` and `xlink:href`, written or resolved from Data.
- The single file of `@gramlot/gramlot-serverless` 0.2.3 allows `'unsafe-eval'`, so inline code runs there too.

## Upgrading from 0.2.2

- Code that changes a code attribute after the start, or inserts nodes with inline code in the live Source, moves to named logic.
- Replace `onclick='…'` and the other `on<event>` attributes with `connect_onclick='…'` and the matching `connect_on<event>`.
- A test that writes inline code in the live Source (`app.builder.root…`) builds its Source on a separate `GramlotBuilder` and mounts it with `startSource`.
- Python: no change for pages; the renderer refuses `on<event>` attributes and `javascript:` URLs.
